+> You are producing non-canonical advisory material only. Per this project's `governance/status-model.md` and the LLM Governance Rules, your output goes into `investigations/` or `proposals/`, is never Canonical, and must not silently resolve an open designer fork. Cite existing DEC IDs from `decision-register.md` where relevant. State your evidence class (mechanical fact / empirical finding / designer ruling / recommendation) for each claim.
+
+# G5 Seven Consuming Mechanics — Candidate Implementations
+
+## 0. Scope and governing constraints
+
+This draft covers exactly the seven consuming mechanics named in **DEC-133.A R3** (designer ruling, non-canonical): **(1) Disengage, (2) Zone of Control, (3) Chase, (4) generic movement contests, (5) Forced Movement magnitude, (6) Pin / Hold Position resolution, (7) Seize / Deny Ground resolution**.
+
+Locked substrate (all claims below labelled per `governance/status-model.md` evidence classes):
+
+- **DEC-133** (designer ruling): canonical spatial model = four abstract bands (Engagement / Short / Medium / Far); Movement Distance per combat turn = effective Movement Speed (`1 Speed = 1 hex`); band↔hex boundaries are content-authoring per **DEC-077.A**; movement measured per combat turn under **DEC-095**. [evidence class: designer ruling]
+- **DEC-133.A R2/R3** (designer ruling): contested-movement consumption is **not ruled**; all seven mechanics remain open as **Position-tier Effects under DEC-023.A**. [evidence class: designer ruling]
+- **DEC-023.A** (designer ruling): Position Tier enumerates Forced Movement; Knock Prone; Seize / Deny Ground; Pin / Hold Position; Open / Close Lane — plus prohibitions: no damage-over-time, no natural-d100 modification (Invariant 6), no new resource pools (Invariant 17), one Effect per win (**DEC-024**). Note: Disengage, Zone of Control, Chase, and "generic movement contests" are **not** in the DEC-023.A alpha list verbatim; this draft treats them as open consuming-mechanic shells that, insofar as they impose consequences, must resolve as Position-tier Effects or as applications of existing contest/reaction machinery — the placement itself is a **recommendation**, not a ruling. [evidence class: designer ruling for the tier list; recommendation for the placement inference]
+- **DEC-095** (designer ruling): one combat turn per round per combatant; one substantive combat action = one S-1 combat exchange (plus nested Active Defense per **DEC-044**); **movement is a free/bundled side-activity that does not consume the substantive action**. [evidence class: designer ruling]
+- **DEC-004 / Canonical §4** (mechanical fact): `Movement Speed = floor((bsp+bss)/15)`; derived statistics are live. [evidence class: mechanical fact]
+- **Invariant 6 / DEC-007 / Canonical §7** (mechanical fact): Cost = natural roll, paid from PE/MP with Overflow→HP. [evidence class: mechanical fact]
+- **DEC-007.A** (designer ruling, canonical amendment): Overflow magnitude/application is immutable — no Tag, Trait, Effect, Condition, or subsystem may reduce, redirect, absorb, or modify it. [evidence class: designer ruling]
+- **Invariant 17** (architectural constraint): no Universal Play subsystem may introduce a competing primary resource or progression economy. [evidence class: architectural constraint]
+- **Invariant 18 / DEC-006** (architectural constraint + mechanical fact): modules must build on the 9-step Core Test Transaction, never replace it. [evidence class: architectural constraint + mechanical fact]
+- **DEC-013 / Canonical §13** (mechanical fact): S-1 is the universal opposed-contest primitive (outcome matrix; Margin/Blackjack/Hybrid Quality; Fail/Fail repeat; exact-tie repeat); each participant pays own Cost, resolves own Failure XP / Doubles / Recovery. [evidence class: mechanical fact]
+- **DEC-024** (designer ruling, cited via DEC-023.A/DEC-095/DEC-106): one Effect per S-1 win. [evidence class: designer ruling]
+- **DEC-107** (designer ruling): Effect Tier = Skill-Tier of the causing skill (max; "equal" default; lesser requires Player choice + GM Fiat); Quality retains tie-break + success-precondition (≥1 floor) only. [evidence class: designer ruling]
+- **DEC-041** (designer ruling): Skill-Tier ≥ 2 production gate for location-referencing Effects. [evidence class: designer ruling]
+- **DEC-115/DEC-117** (designer ruling): unified StateRecord (`Type / Tier Y / Magnitude Z / [Location X]`, `Z = −Y` for Effect/Condition records); counter/removal machinery. [evidence class: designer ruling]
+- **DEC-132 / DEC-132.A / DEC-132.B** (designer ruling): reactions beyond Active Defense permitted when (a) defined trigger, (b) `reaction:` Tag possessed, (c) resolved as full S-1 opposed contest with full Core Test Cost; uncapped; independent of Active Defense; movement-trigger is a ruled trigger *category*, exact menus content-authored per DEC-077.A. [evidence class: designer ruling]
+- **DEC-122 / DEC-138** (designer ruling): movement-penalty expression (self-referential-Y total-lock for Stunned/Incapacitated/Restrained/Grappled/Prone, provisional; uniform `Z = −Y` overlay otherwise; **DEC-004** formula untouched). [evidence class: designer ruling]
+- **DEC-124 / DEC-131** (designer ruling): Grappled move-away = contested Break Hold; fail = locked/no relocation; success = stepwise Heal-Effect-System Tier-mutation removal. Cited as the closest ruled precedent for hold/escape contests. [evidence class: designer ruling]
+- **DEC-130** (designer ruling): GM Fiat is universal in scope, bounded in authority (cannot override Locked Canonical Core). [evidence class: designer ruling]
+
+Consumption principle applied throughout (recommendation, Invariant-17-checked): because **DEC-095** makes uncontested movement a free side-activity and **DEC-133.A R2** leaves contested-movement consumption unruled, this draft proposes that **distance moved is always debited against the mover's per-turn Movement Distance allowance (effective Movement Speed in hexes), and any opposed roll is always a full Core Test / S-1 contest with normal Cost** — i.e. consumption is *distance accounting + ordinary test Cost*, never a new point pool. Whether distance-debit, test-Cost, both, or neither applies per mechanic is left as the explicit fork (see §8). [evidence class: recommendation]
+
+What this draft does **not** do: it does not rule any fork, does not author band↔hex boundaries (content-authoring per DEC-133(4)/DEC-077.A), does not define duration/time-unit scale (G3 remains open per DEC-133.A/DEC-138), and does not create mechanics for Open/Close Lane or Knock Prone beyond their mention as shared-machinery neighbours. [evidence class: designer ruling for the open/content-authoring status; recommendation for the scoping]
+
+---
+
+## 1. Disengage (leaving Engagement)
+
+### (a) Candidate rules text
+
+> **D-0 Common shell (both options).** A combatant that uses its per-turn movement (DEC-095 free side-activity; DEC-133 distance allowance) to leave the *Engagement* band relative to an engaged opponent declares **Disengage**. Distance moved debits the mover's remaining Movement Distance allowance for that turn. Leaving Engagement is a *movement-trigger* (DEC-132.A R1 category); opponents possessing a matching `reaction:` Tag *may* be eligible to react — eligibility and exact Tag vocabulary remain content-authoring (DEC-077.A, DEC-132(4)). All rolls below are full Core Tests / S-1 contests with normal Cost, Overflow, Failure XP, Doubles, Recovery (DEC-006/007/009/012/008). No roll modifier ever touches the natural d100 (Invariant 6); difficulty, if any, is Skill-side per DEC-063 precedent.
+>
+> **Option D-A — Contested Disengage (S-1 gate).** The mover declares the destination (band + hex path within allowance). Each engaged opponent that contests (GM Fiat for which opponents contest, per DEC-106 §2/DEC-130; or all engaged opponents in automated play) resolves one S-1 opposed contest (DEC-013) against the mover: mover rolls the movement Skill (content-authored lineage; e.g. Agility/Quickness-family), opponent rolls a content-authored holding Skill. Mover win (outright or higher Quality on Both-Success) → mover completes the declared move (within allowance); opponent win → mover's exit is arrested at the Engagement edge (distance already travelled up to that edge is still debited; mover retains any unused allowance for non-exiting repositioning). Fail/Fail or exact-tie → repeat per DEC-013 §§13.4–13.5 (each repeat is a fresh full-Cost round). Quality mode default: Margin (efficiency/precision) per DEC-013 §13.3 guidance; GM may override.
+>
+> **Option D-B — Free exit + Reaction window.** The mover completes the declared move within allowance with **no gate contest**. Each engaged opponent with a matching `reaction:vigilant`-family Tag (content-authored) may resolve one Reaction (DEC-132, full S-1 opposed contest, full Cost) against the mover. Reaction winner selects one Position-tier Effect they are entitled to (DEC-023.A list; e.g. Forced Movement to re-engage, Pin/Hold Position attempt, or Base-tier Inflict Injury per DEC-096/104 if the table so entitles) subject to one-Effect-per-win (DEC-024) and Effect-Tier = reactor's Skill-Tier (DEC-107). If no opponent reacts, the exit is unopposed and costs only distance + the mover's own movement-test Cost if the table requires a movement test at all (GM Fiat whether unopposed movement requires any test; DEC-130).
+
+### (b) Evidence class per claim
+
+- Movement is free/bundled side-activity; one S-1 exchange per turn — **designer ruling (DEC-095)**.
+- Distance allowance = effective Movement Speed hexes — **designer ruling (DEC-133)**.
+- Movement-trigger is a ruled reaction category; exact triggers/Tags content-authored — **designer ruling (DEC-132.A R1, DEC-132(4), DEC-077.A)**.
+- S-1 matrix/repeat rules; full Cost per participant — **mechanical fact (DEC-013, DEC-006/007)**.
+- One Effect per win; Effect Tier = causing Skill-Tier — **designer ruling (DEC-024, DEC-107)**.
+- Contested-vs-free shape (D-A vs D-B) — **recommendation** (fork preserved; no ruling exists).
+- Skill-side-only difficulty; no natural-roll modification — **architectural constraint (Invariant 6)** + **recommendation** for the application here.
+
+### (c) Options analysis + invariant check
+
+- Both options satisfy **Invariant 6** (no roll modification; Quality compares already-rolled successes, DEC-013 §13.2) and **Invariant 17** (no movement-point pool; distance-debit is allowance accounting against the DEC-133 statistic, same shape as DEC-069's bookkeeping-not-pool assessment — **recommendation**, assessor to verify).
+- D-A costs more tests (each contest round is full-Cost — death-spiral risk via Overflow; mirrors DEC-131's full-Core-Test contest cost). D-B costs fewer tests but shifts load onto content-authored Tag distribution (tables without the Tag have no disengage pressure — a balance fork for the designer).
+- Neither option modifies Overflow (DEC-007.A) or the DEC-004 formula (DEC-078 A3 discipline).
+
+### Designer questions left open
+
+1. Gate or window (D-A vs D-B, or hybrid: contest only against `reaction:`-Tag holders)?
+2. Which Skill lineages may roll Disengage contests (content-authoring now, or framework-fixed)?
+3. Does a failed D-A exit consume the mover's substantive action, or only movement allowance (DEC-095 interaction)?
+
+---
+
+## 2. Zone of Control (ZoC)
+
+### (a) Candidate rules text
+
+> **Z-0 Common shell.** A Zone of Control is a **declarative, read-only area assertion**: while combatant C is in a stated posture (content-authored; e.g. wielding `handling:reach`, holding a lane), the Engagement-adjacent hexes/band around C are flagged as **controlled**. The flag itself rolls nothing, spends nothing, and creates no pool (DEC-088 Conditional-Trait-Binding grammar precedent: `Active only while [stance/tag] present`). What the flag *enables* is the fork below. Posture declaration breadth (which Tags/Traits may carry a ZoC clause) is content-authoring (DEC-077.A).
+>
+> **Option Z-A — ZoC as Difficult-Ground overlay.** Entering, crossing, or exiting controlled hexes costs **2 hexes of Movement Distance allowance per 1 hex traversed** (cost multiplier on distance accounting, not a new currency). The multiplier is the sole effect; no contest is forced. (At DEC-002 floor discipline: each hex debited as `2`; allowance check per hex entered.) GM Fiat may waive for allies/formation movement (DEC-130).
+>
+> **Option Z-B — ZoC as Reaction-enabler only.** Controlled status grants **no movement-cost change**. Instead, movement through controlled space is a declared movement-trigger to which holders of a matching `reaction:` Tag may react (DEC-132 machinery, one Reaction per reactor per trigger event, each a full S-1 contest at full Cost). Without a reactor Tag + declared reaction, ZoC has no mechanical effect.
+
+### (b) Evidence class per claim
+
+- Read-only/stateless clause pattern creates no pool — **designer ruling precedent (DEC-088, DEC-059)** applied by analogy; the analogy itself is a **recommendation**.
+- `env:terrain_*` descriptive-only vs `env:freezing` activation distinction — **designer ruling (DEC-091, DEC-088)**; ZoC deliberately follows the *activation* pattern, which is a **recommendation**.
+- Distance-multiplier is allowance accounting, not a pool — **recommendation** (requires verifier check against Invariant 17).
+- Reaction shape (full S-1, full Cost, uncapped, independent of Active Defense) — **designer ruling (DEC-132, DEC-132.A R2/R3)**.
+- Posture/Tag menus content-authored — **designer ruling (DEC-077.A, DEC-132(4))**.
+
+### (c) Options analysis + invariant check
+
+- Z-A risks an **Invariant 6** misread (a "×2 cost" could be mistaken for Cost modification): this draft scopes the multiplier strictly to *hex-allowance debit*, never to PE/MP Cost — flagged for verifier attention. No natural-roll, Cost, Overflow, or Recovery value is altered — **recommendation**, believed Invariant-6/DEC-007.A-safe.
+- Z-B is the minimal-architecture option (reuses only already-ruled machinery) but makes ZoC vacuous on tables without authored Tags.
+- A hybrid (multiplier + reactions) is **not** proposed as default (stacking burden); listed as a designer-combinable fork, not a recommendation.
+
+### Designer questions left open
+
+1. Cost-multiplier (Z-A), reaction-enabler (Z-B), or neither (ZoC dropped as a named mechanic, subsumed by Seize/Deny Ground)?
+2. If Z-A: multiplier value content-authored or framework-fixed at 2-for-1?
+3. Does ZoC affect allies (selective vs indiscriminate)?
+
+---
+
+## 3. Chase (pursuit over multiple turns)
+
+### (a) Candidate rules text
+
+> **C-0 Common shell.** A Chase is declared when (a) a quarry leaves Short band toward Medium/Far (DEC-133 bands) and (b) at least one pursuer declares pursuit. Bands are qualitative (DEC-133(4)); hex positions remain the authoritative distance record. The Chase ends when pursuer and quarry share Engagement (caught), the quarry exceeds an authored lead threshold / exits the scene (escaped), or all pursuers abandon (GM Fiat, DEC-130).
+>
+> **Option C-A — Extended-Test Margin race.** The Chase is an Extended Test (DEC-067/068/070 machinery): each round, each runner makes an ordinary movement Core Test (full Cost); each **success** banks its Margin (`Skill − Roll`) into that runner's private running total; failures bank nothing and are otherwise neutral on progress (DEC-068). Totals are monotonically non-decreasing running tallies, never spent — the DEC-069 bookkeeping-not-pool shape. Catch/escape thresholds are GM-set per instance (DEC-070, no formula). Relative lead = quarry total − pursuer total, mapped to bands/hexes by GM judgement (no fixed conversion — G3/band-boundary content gap acknowledged).
+>
+> **Option C-B — Repeated S-1 movement contests.** Each round, pursuer and quarry resolve one S-1 opposed movement contest (DEC-013, full Cost each). Winner's Margin ( DEC-013 §13.2 Margin mode) converts to **lead change in hexes**: `lead_delta = winner_Margin − loser_Margin_if_loser_also_succeeded_else_0`, floored at 0, debited/credited against current separation (never below 0 = caught). Fail/Fail → no lead change, repeat next round (each round's tests already fully costed). Contest-delta shape mirrors the ruled DEC-104 HP-delta precedent by analogy (analogy is a recommendation, not a ruling).
+
+### (b) Evidence class per claim
+
+- Bands qualitative; hex authoritative; boundaries content-authored — **designer ruling (DEC-133(4), DEC-077.A)**.
+- Margin-accumulation / neutral-failure / GM-set target — **designer ruling (DEC-067, DEC-068, DEC-070)**.
+- Margin totals are not a pool — **architectural-constraint assessment precedent (DEC-069)**; extension to Chase is a **recommendation**.
+- S-1 universal primitive; full Cost both sides — **mechanical fact (DEC-013, DEC-006/007)**.
+- Contest-delta for HP (DEC-104) exists; hex-delta for lead is **recommendation by analogy**.
+
+### (c) Options analysis + invariant check
+
+- C-A reuses the most already-ruled machinery (zero new concepts) but needs per-instance GM thresholds (DEC-070 burden every chase).
+- C-B gives spatial immediacy (hexes move on the map) but introduces a **new conversion (Margin → hexes)** that has no ruled precedent (DEC-104 converts Margin → HP only) — flagged as the draft's largest invention; verifier should treat it as **recommendation requiring designer approval**.
+- Both satisfy Invariant 6 (Margins derive from Skill-side values; rolls untouched) and Invariant 17 on the DEC-069 reading (tallies/lead are positional bookkeeping, never spent).
+
+### Designer questions left open
+
+1. Race (C-A) vs per-round contests (C-B)?
+2. If C-B: Margin→hex conversion formula, or GM judgement per round?
+3. Does difficult terrain / ZoC (Z-A) interact with Chase totals, lead, or neither?
+
+---
+
+## 4. Generic movement contests (the shared primitive)
+
+### (a) Candidate rules text
+
+> **M-0 Primitive.** Any contested repositioning not covered by §§1–3, 6–7 resolves as **one S-1 opposed contest** (DEC-013) between mover and contestant, each a full Core Test (DEC-006). Default Quality: **Margin** (precision/efficiency); Blackjack/Hybrid available by GM override per DEC-013 §13.3 (force/commitment framing). Winner imposes their declared movement outcome within the mover's remaining allowance; loser imposes nothing (DEC-101 defender-wins precedent applied by analogy: contest loser gains no counter-Effect — **recommendation**). Fail/Fail and exact-tie repeat per DEC-013 (fresh full-Cost rounds). Eligibility to contest a given move (who may roll, how many contestants, GM Fiat vs all-engaged) is **not** fixed here — see per-mechanic text and designer question 1.
+>
+> **Option M-A — Contest consumes allowance only.** The contest itself costs each side only its ordinary Core Test Cost (DEC-007); the *movement* consumes the mover's distance allowance on success. The contestant spends no distance.
+>
+> **Option M-B — Contest consumes allowance symmetrically.** Winner's imposed repositioning debits **both** parties' allowances equivalently (drag-along / scramble shape): each hex of imposed movement debits 1 hex from each participant's remaining allowance; a party with insufficient allowance cannot be compelled beyond its remainder (excess is truncated, GM narrates the shortfall).
+
+### (b) Evidence class per claim
+
+- S-1 primitive, Quality menu + GM override, repeat rules, own-Cost — **mechanical fact (DEC-013)**.
+- Defender-wins-no-counter-Effect — **designer ruling (DEC-101)** for opposed *attacks*; extension to movement contests is a **recommendation**.
+- M-A vs M-B consumption shapes — **recommendation** (this is the DEC-133.A R2 fork, explicitly unruled).
+
+### (c) Options analysis + invariant check
+
+- This section **is** the DEC-133.A R2 consumption fork in miniature; it must not be resolved here — both options are carried to §8 verbatim.
+- M-B's symmetric debit is still allowance accounting (no pool), but doubles the bookkeeping and can strand slow contestants at 0 allowance — a play-feel fork for the designer.
+- Invariant 6/DEC-007.A clean under both (no roll/Cost/Overflow alteration).
+
+### Designer questions left open
+
+1. Standing contest-eligibility rule (all engaged may contest vs GM-Fiat selection vs Tag-gated)?
+2. M-A vs M-B as the universal default (per-mechanic overrides allowed)?
+
+---
+
+## 5. Forced Movement magnitude
+
+### (a) Candidate rules text
+
+> **F-0 Common shell.** Forced Movement is a Position-tier Effect (DEC-023.A) selected on an S-1 win (DEC-024), imposed on the loser. Direction is declared by the winner (push/pull/slide); destination legality (walls, hazards, off-scene) is GM Fiat (DEC-130); hazardous destinations do not themselves add damage under current design (no-DoT policy, DEC-023.A; fall/hazard dice explicitly unruled — must not be silently substituted into Overflow per DEC-091 qualification).
+>
+> **Option F-A — Tier-equals-hexes.** Displacement in hexes = the Effect's Tier (`Y`, which under DEC-107 equals the causing Skill's Skill-Tier by default). Direction declared by winner; path blocked → stop at obstruction (excess lost). Record (if duration needed, e.g. continued slide): standard StateRecord `Type: Forced-Movement / Tier Y / Magnitude Z` with `Z = −Y` per DEC-115 R2 (magnitude retained for Heal-System interaction symmetry although displacement itself uses `Y` — flagged duality, see questions).
+>
+> **Option F-B — Margin-mediated displacement.** Displacement = Effect Tier (F-A base) **plus** `floor(winner_Margin / 10)` bonus hexes (Margin = winner's `Skill − Roll` on the winning test; divisor 10 keeps numbers within DEC-133 hex economy; divisor value is recommendation-only). Margin bonus never exceeds +3 hexes (cap is recommendation-only, anti-spike). All Margin inputs are post-mitigation-survivor values where Active Defense applied (DEC-103/104 channel separation respected: HP delta and Effect shred resolve first; displacement applies from the surviving Effect).
+
+### (b) Evidence class per claim
+
+- Forced Movement is Position-tier; one Effect per win — **designer ruling (DEC-023.A, DEC-024)**.
+- Effect Tier = causing Skill-Tier — **designer ruling (DEC-107)**.
+- `Z = −Y` record shape — **designer ruling (DEC-115 R2)**.
+- Margin = `Skill − Roll`; winner's Margin as HP magnitude — **designer ruling (DEC-096/104)** for HP; reuse for hexes is **recommendation**.
+- Hazard-damage prohibition — **designer ruling (DEC-023.A no-DoT; DEC-091 qualification)**.
+- F-A vs F-B — **recommendation** (fork preserved).
+
+### (c) Options analysis + invariant check
+
+- F-A is minimal (no new formula; Tier already exists on every Effect). F-B adds high-roll reward but couples displacement to Margin, which Active Defense already de-escalates (DEC-103) — interaction complexity is the cost.
+- Both Invariant-6-safe (Margin/ Tier are Skill-side derivations). Invariant-17-safe (hexes are positional facts, not a spendable pool).
+- Open duality flagged: DEC-115 says Effect Magnitude `Z = −Y`, but displacement wants a *positive* hex count from `Y` — this draft reads displacement off Tier, not Magnitude, preserving DEC-115 verbatim. Whether that reading is correct is a **designer question**, not a ruling.
+
+### Designer questions left open
+
+1. Tier-only (F-A) vs Tier + Margin bonus (F-B)?
+2. If F-B: divisor and cap values?
+3. Confirm Tier-vs-Magnitude reading (displacement off `Y`) or rule otherwise?
+4. Does forced movement debit the *target's* remaining allowance, the *winner's*, or neither (R2 fork)?
+
+---
+
+## 6. Pin / Hold Position resolution
+
+### (a) Candidate rules text
+
+> **P-0 Common shell.** Pin / Hold Position is a Position-tier Effect (DEC-023.A) that arrests a target in place. Imposition requires an S-1 win with the Effect selected (DEC-024); Effect Tier = causing Skill-Tier (DEC-107). The record is a standard StateRecord (`Type: Pin/Hold / Tier Y / Magnitude Z = −Y / [Location X optional]`, DEC-115). While held, the target's effective Movement Speed interaction follows existing Condition machinery by analogy (DEC-122/138 shape) — exact zero-vs-penalty treatment is a fork below, **not** ruled here. Release follows the DEC-131 stepwise shape by analogy (see options).
+>
+> **Option P-A — Hard lock + Break-Hold escape (DEC-131 mirror).** Imposition zeroes the target's arrestable movement (DEC-122 self-referential-Y shape applied as Position Effect by analogy). Escape requires a contested Break Hold / Break Free S-1 contest (DEC-124 machinery): fail → hold persists, no relocation; success → stepwise Tier-mutation (`Y −= 1` per success, `Z` recalcs, gate = breaker's Skill-Tier ≥ record's current Tier per DEC-121/DEC-035.A cl.5 shape); `Y = 0` removes the record and frees the mover. Each contest is a full Core Test (DEC-006/DEC-123 shape).
+>
+> **Option P-B — Soft lock (Skill-side + allowance clamp).** Imposition does **not** zero movement. Instead: (i) target's movement-skill Effective Skill suffers Skill-side penalty equal to the record's Tier (DEC-063/DEC-079 C4 pattern, Skill-side only — Invariant 6 preserved); (ii) target's per-turn distance allowance is clamped to `max(0, effective Movement Speed − Y)` hexes while the record persists. Escape is either (a) winning any movement contest (M-0) against the holder despite the penalties, or (b) DEC-121 Tier-mutation via a qualifying Skill Test — both routes available (DEC-135.A R2 two-route precedent applied by analogy).
+
+### (b) Evidence class per claim
+
+- Position-tier placement; one Effect per win; Tier = Skill-Tier — **designer ruling (DEC-023.A, DEC-024, DEC-107)**.
+- StateRecord shape; Tier-mutation; Skill-Tier gate — **designer ruling (DEC-115, DEC-121, DEC-035.A cl.5)**.
+- Grappled Break-Hold fail-persists / stepwise-removal shape — **designer ruling (DEC-124, DEC-131)** for Grappled; extension to Pin/Hold is **recommendation by analogy**.
+- Skill-side-only penalty pattern — **designer ruling precedent (DEC-063, DEC-079 C4, DEC-072.A)**; application here is **recommendation**.
+- Two-route removal precedent — **designer ruling (DEC-135.A R2)** for Fatigued; extension here is **recommendation**.
+- P-A vs P-B — **recommendation** (fork preserved).
+
+### (c) Options analysis + invariant check
+
+- P-A reuses the nearest ruled neighbour verbatim (Grappled) — lowest invention, but hard-locks can stall slow characters (DEC-125's anti-zero precedent noted: consider a `max(1,…)`-style clamp if P-A is chosen — **recommendation**, designer to rule).
+- P-B is gentler and keeps movement meaningful under a hold, but introduces an allowance-clamp formula with no direct precedent (verifier: Invariant-17 check — clamp is a ceiling on allowance use, not a pool).
+- Both Invariant-6/DEC-007.A-clean.
+
+### Designer questions left open
+
+1. Hard lock (P-A) vs soft lock (P-B)?
+2. Does Pin/Hold require a Location (limb/ground) or is it global (DEC-115 optional-Location)?
+3. Relation to Grappled/Restrained Conditions (distinct identities per DEC-023.A(3) — is Pin a third identity or a Position-flavoured Grapple)?
+
+---
+
+## 7. Seize / Deny Ground resolution
+
+### (a) Candidate rules text
+
+> **G-0 Common shell.** Seize / Deny Ground is a Position-tier Effect (DEC-023.A) contesting *control of ground* rather than *possession of a body* (the Pin/Hold contrast). Imposition requires an S-1 win with the Effect selected (DEC-024); Effect Tier = causing Skill-Tier (DEC-107). The record marks ground, not the character: StateRecord (`Type: Seized/Denied-Ground / Tier Y / Magnitude Z = −Y / Location X = contested hexes-or-band`, DEC-115 with mandatory Location — **recommendation**). Control confers no HP, no XP, no pool — only the movement consequences below.
+>
+> **Option G-A — Denial-field (entry contest).** While the record persists, any opponent entering the marked ground must first win an S-1 movement contest (M-0) against the record holder (or against the record's Tier as a passive difficulty — fork G-A1 active-holder vs G-A2 standing-record; default proposed: active-holder contest, G-A1). Failure → entry refused at the field edge (distance to edge still debited). Allies of the holder pass freely unless the holder declares otherwise (GM Fiat default: selective — **recommendation**).
+>
+> **Option G-B — Advantage-ground (Skill-side edge).** Marked ground grants no entry barrier. Instead, the holder (and declared allies) gains a Skill-side bonus / the intruder suffers a Skill-side penalty of `±Y` (record's Tier) on movement contests (M-0) and on attacks made from/within the marked ground (DEC-063 Skill-side pattern; never on the natural roll). Control changes hands when an intruder wins a contest *while physically inside* the marked ground — winner authors a replacement record at their own Effect Tier (higher Tier replaces per DEC-079 stacking-pattern precedent applied by analogy).
+
+### (b) Evidence class per claim
+
+- Position-tier placement; one Effect per win; Tier = Skill-Tier — **designer ruling (DEC-023.A, DEC-024, DEC-107)**.
+- StateRecord with Location — **designer ruling (DEC-115 R1)** permits optional Location; *mandatory*-Location for ground records is **recommendation**.
+- Skill-side-only modifiers — **designer ruling precedent (DEC-063)**; application here **recommendation**.
+- Same-tier-add / higher-replaces stacking shape — **designer ruling (DEC-079 alpha vocabulary; DEC-135 F4)**; extension to ground records **recommendation**.
+- G-A vs G-B (barrier vs edge) — **recommendation** (fork preserved).
+
+### (c) Options analysis + invariant check
+
+- G-A creates hard battlefield geometry (strong control fantasy; risk of stalemate at chokepoints). G-B is softer (no refusal; control matters at contest time only).
+- Both Invariant-6-clean (Skill-side only) and Invariant-17-clean (ground marks are positional facts with counter/removal via DEC-117 R3–R5-equivalent handling — removal Tags / Tier-mutation; exact removal route is a designer question).
+- G-A2 (standing-record passive difficulty) would need a difficulty-grade value (DEC-063) — not specified here; flagged as requiring a further ruling if chosen.
+
+### Designer questions left open
+
+1. Barrier (G-A) vs edge (G-B)?
+2. If G-A: active-holder contest (G-A1) vs standing-record difficulty (G-A2)?
+3. Mandatory Location on ground records (proposed) vs optional?
+4. Removal route: Tier-mutation only, contest-takeover only, or both? Duration default (`scene` per DEC-117 R2 Effect default — **recommendation**, not ruling)?
+
+---
+
+## 8. Cross-cutting consumption ruling (the DEC-133.A R2 fork, preserved)
+
+The single question DEC-133.A R2 leaves open — *what does contested movement consume?* — appears in every section above. It is **not resolved** by this draft. The candidate positions:
+
+| Position | Shape | Satisfies Inv. 6 / 17 on this draft's reading (verifier to confirm) |
+|---|---|---|
+| R2-A Distance-only | Contests cost only ordinary Core Test Cost (DEC-007); movement debits mover's allowance | Yes / Yes |
+| R2-B Symmetric distance | Imposed movement debits both parties (M-B) | Yes / Yes (bookkeeping) |
+| R2-C Test-Cost-only | Movement itself is costless beyond the tests' natural-roll Cost; allowance not debited for contested moves | Yes / Yes |
+| R2-D Both | Distance debit + full test Cost for every contest round | Yes / Yes (harshest economy; Overflow-spiral risk flagged as **empirical-finding-to-be**: needs playtest, not asserted) |
+
+**Recommendation (not a ruling):** adopt R2-A as the default with per-mechanic overrides (M-B where scramble fiction demands it), because it is the smallest delta over DEC-095 + DEC-133: free movement already debits nothing but distance, and tests already cost what tests cost. [evidence class: recommendation]
+
+---
+
+## 9. Consolidated designer question list (G1 gate input)
+
+1. Disengage: D-A (contest gate) vs D-B (free exit + reactions)?
+2. ZoC: Z-A (cost multiplier) vs Z-B (reaction-enabler) vs drop?
+3. Chase: C-A (Extended-Test race) vs C-B (repeated S-1, Margin→hex conversion)?
+4. Generic contests: standing eligibility rule; M-A vs M-B default?
+5. Forced Movement: F-A (Tier = hexes) vs F-B (Tier + Margin bonus, divisor/cap values)? Confirm Tier-vs-Magnitude reading. Whose allowance is debited?
+6. Pin/Hold: P-A (hard lock + Break-Hold) vs P-B (soft lock + clamp)? Identity vs Grappled/Restrained? Location required?
+7. Seize/Deny: G-A (barrier) vs G-B (edge)? G-A1 vs G-A2? Mandatory Location? Removal route + duration default?
+8. R2 consumption: R2-A/B/C/D as universal default?
+9. Skill lineages for movement contests: framework-fixed or content-authored (DEC-077.A)?
+10. Margin→hex and allowance-clamp formulas (§§3, 6): framework values or content-authored?
+
+No alternative above is preferred by this draft beyond the explicitly-labelled R2-A lean in §8, which is itself a recommendation only. All forks require designer ruling (gate G1); any promotion toward Canonical additionally requires the 8-step Promotion Rule (gate G2).
+
+---
+
+## 10. Traceability
+
+- Core Invariants: `canonical/rules/tiwas-canonical-rules-and-changelog-v1.3.md` §16 (Invariants 6, 17, 18).
+- Spatial substrate + open list: `decision-register.md` DEC-133, DEC-133.A (R2, R3).
+- Position-tier placement + prohibitions: DEC-023.A; one-Effect-per-win: DEC-024.
+- Turn/movement economy: DEC-095; Movement Speed: DEC-004.
+- Contest primitive: DEC-013 (Canonical §13); Core Transaction + Cost/Overflow/Recovery/XP/Doubles: DEC-006/007/007.A/008/009/012.
+- Effect Tier/Magnitude/records: DEC-107, DEC-115/116/117, DEC-121, DEC-035.A.
+- Reactions: DEC-132/132.A/132.B. Holds/escapes: DEC-124/131. Penalties: DEC-122/138, DEC-063/064. Fiat: DEC-130. Content-authoring: DEC-077.A. Location gates: DEC-041.

13: 
14: # Tiwas GDD — Multi-LLM Orchestration Plan
15: 
16: **Document Version:** v0.1
17: **Document Status:** Advisory implementation/process guidance
18: **Rule Authority:** None — this document does not create game mechanics
19: **No DEC inferred.** This is a workflow plan, not a designer ruling.
20: **Important:** Implementation guidance must never be mistaken for a design ruling. No output produced under this plan is authoritative until the designer accepts it (gate G1) and, where canonical status is sought, the 8-step Promotion Rule completes (gate G2).
21: 
22: ## 0. Purpose
23: 
24: Rapidly develop the Game Development Document (GDD) — a structured outline/backbone of Tiwas (section structure, dependency graph, locked invariants, open questions) — by filling sections in parallel with multiple AI agents running across several API-based models. The plan chooses a control plane (opencode CLI, OpenChamber, or both), assigns specialised roles, and keeps the designer as the final human gate.
25: 
26: This document exists separately from the rules so that:
27: 
28: - drafting speed does not become game law;
29: - cross-LLM contradictions are surfaced as designer questions, not silently resolved;
30: - future LLM sessions have a stable, reusable development process; and
31: - provenance and promotion discipline remain enforceable.
32: 
33: ## 1. Why multi-LLM
34: 
35: GDD work is two different labour types.
36: 
37: - **Divergent generation** — alternative framings for open subsystems (S-2..S-12 candidates). Parallelism pays hard here: N models surface N candidate designs, and cross-model disagreement is exactly the question list the designer must rule on.
38: - **Convergent unification** — invariant-checking, dependency ordering, merging, governance. This must be one disciplined agent with the repository in context; otherwise the result is five self-consistent but mutually contradictory doclets.
39: 
40: Rule of thumb: **front-end parallel, back-end serial.** Parallelism is spent on leaf sections of the dependency DAG, never on merge points.
41: 
42: ## 2. Division of labour / agent roster
43: 
44: | Agent | Who / what | Job |
45: |---|---|---|
46: | Backbone Builder / Orchestrator | opencode (this environment) | Build spec cards, edit repository files, obey governance, perform final merges |
47: | Drafter pool | 3–5 different-vendor models | First-pass section content, alternative mechanic framings |
48: | Adversarial Verifier | One strong model NOT in the drafter pool | Red-team drafts against spec-card invariants + decision register; flag silent assumptions and contradictions |
49: | Synthesizer / Fusion | OpenChamber Fusion → opencode finalizes | Combine strongest parts; surviving disagreements become the human-question list |
50: | Registrar | opencode | Provenance headers, DEC references, decision-register annotations |
51: | Designer | Tiwa | Rulings only (gates G1 and G2) |
52: 
53: Verifier independence is deliberate: a model that drafted a section must not also vouch for it.
54: 
55: ## 3. The pipeline
56: 
57: - **P0 — Backbone (opencode).** Extract the GDD skeleton from the Canonical Rules (`canonical/rules/tiwas-canonical-rules-and-changelog-v1.3.md`), the roadmap, and the decision register (`_consolidation/decision-register.md`). One **spec card per section** = purpose, status, dependency chain, locked invariants, open questions, links (DEC / proposal / investigation). The spec card is the *contract* a drafter agent must satisfy.
58: - **P1 — Draft sprint (OpenChamber Multi-run).** Pick a ready leaf section; dispatch one prompt to 3–5 models, each in its own git worktree (zero collisions). Outcomes: N candidates.
59: - **P2 — Verify (Verifier).** Each candidate checked against spec-card invariants and the decision register → pass/fail + contradiction report.
60: - **P3 — Merge (opencode).** Keep the best, or Fusion the survivors; contradictions become the question list.
61: - **P4 — Human gate (G1).** Designer rules on the question list → adopt into the GDD working copy. Anything seeking canonical status then runs the existing proposal → DEC → 8-step Promotion path (G2). The GDD working document stays advisory until formal promotion.
62: 
63: Loop: a queue of leaf sections is drained by OpenChamber **scheduled tasks**; every drafting session gets a **Session Goal** («fill section to spec card v2; keep going until the invariant check passes»).
64: 
65: ## 4. OpenChamber — what to use it for, concretely
66: 
67: OpenChamber is an MIT-licensed, open-source **visual control room on top of the OpenCode SDK — the same agent engine opencode uses.** It adds the supervision layer a single terminal lacks: parallel multi-model runs, Fusion, session goals, scheduling, diff walkthroughs, remote review. Version 1.23.2 is installed globally on the workstation (npm), so no new infrastructure is required.
68: 
69: | Feature | Project step |
70: |---|---|
71: | Multi-run (1 task → up to 5 models, worktree isolation) | P1 draft sprints |
72: | Fusion (combine strongest parts) | P3 merge input |
73: | Session Goals (continue toward a finish line, even with app closed) | Each section-fill session |
74: | Scheduled tasks (cron) | Nightly consistency audit of GDD vs decision register |
75: | Changes Walkthrough (AI-guided diff tour) | Review of merged backbone before G1 |
76: | Agent Control tool (agents create sessions from chat) | «Spin up a Sprint session for S-7 on gpt/gemini/claude» |
77: | Remote (browser/phone, QR + private relay) | Rule on question lists while away; end-to-end encrypted |
78: 
79: **One-time configuration.** Settings → Providers: paste API keys per vendor; use *Other/Custom* (base URL + key or `{env:VAR}`) for OpenAI-compatible endpoints (Ollama, LiteLLM). Settings → Agents: recreate the roster in §2 (model, temperature, standing instructions, tool rules). Agent definitions are stored through OpenCode, so they are shared with the opencode CLI — one setup, two surfaces.
80: 
81: **Caveats.** Single-maintainer project (fast-moving, so keep the opencode-CLI path as the control fallback); not an IDE (pair with the VS Code extension where useful); inference cost = the provider keys (the dashboard shows token use and cost per session).
82: 
83: ## 5. Consistency & governance gates
84: 
85: - Spec cards are the contract. The Verifier rejects violations mechanically, not by taste.
86: - A terminology glossary is maintained by opencode; the Verifier checks keyword consistency across drafts.
87: - Provenance rules (`governance/provenance.md`) apply: `author_llm` / `assessor_llm` / `last_modified_by_llm` / dates per model; no overwriting of original authorship; unknown provenance recorded as unknown.
88: - **G1 and G2 are non-negotiable.** No LLM ever promotes, demotes, supersedes, or resolves rule authority. Ambiguous authority questions are escalated to the designer, never guessed.
89: - No authority inference from chronology, version number, filename, or detail — per repository governance.
90: 
91: ## 6. Tool & model plan
92: 
93: - Control planes: OpenChamber (visual supervision, parallel runs) + opencode CLI (authoritative repository edits, merges, governance).
94: - Drafter pool: maximise vendor divergence — e.g. Claude + GPT + Gemini + Grok + one cheap/open model (LiteLLM / Ollama) for volume. Verifier: a strong model absent from the pool. Orchestrator: opencode's configured model.
95: - Fixtures: reuse existing cross-LLM playtest harnesses and exchange logs as regression material for consistency checks. Spec cards remain markdown-first to match repository conventions.
96: - Isolation: one git worktree per Multi-run; a single *integration* worktree for merges.
97: 
98: ## 7. First-week path
99: 
100: - **Day 0 (designer):** open OpenChamber, connect providers, recreate the §2 agent roster.
101: - **Day 0 (opencode):** produce the backbone + spec cards for the first three leaf sections; designer approves the spec-card template.
102: - **Day 1:** first Multi-run sprint on one section (3 models) → Verifier → merge → G1 ruling → template is proven.
103: - **Day 2:** Session Goal + nightly scheduled audit live; second sprint; GDD conflict register opened.
104: - **Days 3–5:** drain the leaf queue; nightly audits; weekly checkpoint with designer question lists.
105: - Exit criterion: template proven on three sections → scale to the full backbone.
106: 
107: ## 8. Failure modes
108: 
109: - **Contradiction drift** → killed by spec cards + Verifier contradiction reports; ambiguity escalates, never resolved by the swarm.
110: - **Coincident error** (several models agree on a wrong take) → 3+ model Fusion + G1 gate.
111: - **Token burn / open-ended drift** → Session Goals with «stop when invariant passes» limits + cost dashboard.
112: - **GDD blending into canonical** → provenance + G1/G2 enforcement; the GDD stays advisory.
113: - **Single-maintainer risk** → nothing critical lives only in OpenChamber; opencode CLI covers the same SDK.
114: - **Backbone mistake** → cheap and early: the nightly audit vs the roadmap re-opens a spec card before content accrues on it.

# Tiwas GDD — Multi-LLM Orchestration Plan

**Document Version:** v0.1
**Document Status:** Advisory implementation/process guidance
**Rule Authority:** None — this document does not create game mechanics
**No DEC inferred.** This is a workflow plan, not a designer ruling.
**Important:** Implementation guidance must never be mistaken for a design ruling. No output produced under this plan is authoritative until the designer accepts it (gate G1) and, where canonical status is sought, the 8-step Promotion Rule completes (gate G2).

## 0. Purpose

Rapidly develop the Game Development Document (GDD) — a structured outline/backbone of Tiwas (section structure, dependency graph, locked invariants, open questions) — by filling sections in parallel with multiple AI agents running across several API-based models. The plan chooses a control plane (opencode CLI, OpenChamber, or both), assigns specialised roles, and keeps the designer as the final human gate.

This document exists separately from the rules so that:

- drafting speed does not become game law;
- cross-LLM contradictions are surfaced as designer questions, not silently resolved;
- future LLM sessions have a stable, reusable development process; and
- provenance and promotion discipline remain enforceable.

## 1. Why multi-LLM

GDD work is two different labour types.

- **Divergent generation** — alternative framings for open subsystems (S-2..S-12 candidates). Parallelism pays hard here: N models surface N candidate designs, and cross-model disagreement is exactly the question list the designer must rule on.
- **Convergent unification** — invariant-checking, dependency ordering, merging, governance. This must be one disciplined agent with the repository in context; otherwise the result is five self-consistent but mutually contradictory doclets.

Rule of thumb: **front-end parallel, back-end serial.** Parallelism is spent on leaf sections of the dependency DAG, never on merge points.

## 2. Division of labour / agent roster

| Agent | Who / what | Job |
|---|---|---|
| Backbone Builder / Orchestrator | opencode (this environment) | Build spec cards, edit repository files, obey governance, perform final merges |
| Drafter pool | 3–5 different-vendor models | First-pass section content, alternative mechanic framings |
| Adversarial Verifier | One strong model NOT in the drafter pool | Red-team drafts against spec-card invariants + decision register; flag silent assumptions and contradictions |
| Synthesizer / Fusion | OpenChamber Fusion → opencode finalizes | Combine strongest parts; surviving disagreements become the human-question list |
| Registrar | opencode | Provenance headers, DEC references, decision-register annotations |
| Designer | Tiwa | Rulings only (gates G1 and G2) |

Verifier independence is deliberate: a model that drafted a section must not also vouch for it.

## 3. The pipeline

- **P0 — Backbone (opencode).** Extract the GDD skeleton from the Canonical Rules (`canonical/rules/tiwas-canonical-rules-and-changelog-v1.3.md`), the roadmap, and the decision register (`_consolidation/decision-register.md`). One **spec card per section** = purpose, status, dependency chain, locked invariants, open questions, links (DEC / proposal / investigation). The spec card is the *contract* a drafter agent must satisfy.
- **P1 — Draft sprint (OpenChamber Multi-run).** Pick a ready leaf section; dispatch one prompt to 3–5 models, each in its own git worktree (zero collisions). Outcomes: N candidates.
- **P2 — Verify (Verifier).** Each candidate checked against spec-card invariants and the decision register → pass/fail + contradiction report.
- **P3 — Merge (opencode).** Keep the best, or Fusion the survivors; contradictions become the question list.
- **P4 — Human gate (G1).** Designer rules on the question list → adopt into the GDD working copy. Anything seeking canonical status then runs the existing proposal → DEC → 8-step Promotion path (G2). The GDD working document stays advisory until formal promotion.

Loop: a queue of leaf sections is drained by OpenChamber **scheduled tasks**; every drafting session gets a **Session Goal** («fill section to spec card v2; keep going until the invariant check passes»).

## 4. OpenChamber — what to use it for, concretely

OpenChamber is an MIT-licensed, open-source **visual control room on top of the OpenCode SDK — the same agent engine opencode uses.** It adds the supervision layer a single terminal lacks: parallel multi-model runs, Fusion, session goals, scheduling, diff walkthroughs, remote review. Version 1.23.2 is installed globally on the workstation (npm), so no new infrastructure is required.

| Feature | Project step |
|---|---|
| Multi-run (1 task → up to 5 models, worktree isolation) | P1 draft sprints |
| Fusion (combine strongest parts) | P3 merge input |
| Session Goals (continue toward a finish line, even with app closed) | Each section-fill session |
| Scheduled tasks (cron) | Nightly consistency audit of GDD vs decision register |
| Changes Walkthrough (AI-guided diff tour) | Review of merged backbone before G1 |
| Agent Control tool (agents create sessions from chat) | «Spin up a Sprint session for S-7 on gpt/gemini/claude» |
| Remote (browser/phone, QR + private relay) | Rule on question lists while away; end-to-end encrypted |

**One-time configuration.** Settings → Providers: paste API keys per vendor; use *Other/Custom* (base URL + key or `{env:VAR}`) for OpenAI-compatible endpoints (Ollama, LiteLLM). Settings → Agents: recreate the roster in §2 (model, temperature, standing instructions, tool rules). Agent definitions are stored through OpenCode, so they are shared with the opencode CLI — one setup, two surfaces.

**Caveats.** Single-maintainer project (fast-moving, so keep the opencode-CLI path as the control fallback); not an IDE (pair with the VS Code extension where useful); inference cost = the provider keys (the dashboard shows token use and cost per session).

## 5. Consistency & governance gates

- Spec cards are the contract. The Verifier rejects violations mechanically, not by taste.
- A terminology glossary is maintained by opencode; the Verifier checks keyword consistency across drafts.
- Provenance rules (`governance/provenance.md`) apply: `author_llm` / `assessor_llm` / `last_modified_by_llm` / dates per model; no overwriting of original authorship; unknown provenance recorded as unknown.
- **G1 and G2 are non-negotiable.** No LLM ever promotes, demotes, supersedes, or resolves rule authority. Ambiguous authority questions are escalated to the designer, never guessed.
- No authority inference from chronology, version number, filename, or detail — per repository governance.

## 6. Tool & model plan

- Control planes: OpenChamber (visual supervision, parallel runs) + opencode CLI (authoritative repository edits, merges, governance).
- Drafter pool: maximise vendor divergence — e.g. Claude + GPT + Gemini + Grok + one cheap/open model (LiteLLM / Ollama) for volume. Verifier: a strong model absent from the pool. Orchestrator: opencode's configured model.
- Fixtures: reuse existing cross-LLM playtest harnesses and exchange logs as regression material for consistency checks. Spec cards remain markdown-first to match repository conventions.
- Isolation: one git worktree per Multi-run; a single *integration* worktree for merges.

## 7. First-week path

- **Day 0 (designer):** open OpenChamber, connect providers, recreate the §2 agent roster.
- **Day 0 (opencode):** produce the backbone + spec cards for the first three leaf sections; designer approves the spec-card template.
- **Day 1:** first Multi-run sprint on one section (3 models) → Verifier → merge → G1 ruling → template is proven.
- **Day 2:** Session Goal + nightly scheduled audit live; second sprint; GDD conflict register opened.
- **Days 3–5:** drain the leaf queue; nightly audits; weekly checkpoint with designer question lists.
- Exit criterion: template proven on three sections → scale to the full backbone.

## 8. Failure modes

- **Contradiction drift** → killed by spec cards + Verifier contradiction reports; ambiguity escalates, never resolved by the swarm.
- **Coincident error** (several models agree on a wrong take) → 3+ model Fusion + G1 gate.
- **Token burn / open-ended drift** → Session Goals with «stop when invariant passes» limits + cost dashboard.
- **GDD blending into canonical** → provenance + G1/G2 enforcement; the GDD stays advisory.
- **Single-maintainer risk** → nothing critical lives only in OpenChamber; opencode CLI covers the same SDK.
- **Backbone mistake** → cheap and early: the nightly audit vs the roadmap re-opens a spec card before content accrues on it.

## 9. Open items / flagged guesses (recorded at v0.1)

1. GDD section scope — drafted for an *outline/backbone* target. If the GDD is intended to become a full canonical ruleset, G2 becomes the bottleneck and the pipeline phases change.
2. Verifier model pick — left open (depends on available keys); requirement is only that it is not in the drafter pool.
3. Spec-card format — markdown-first assumed; JSON/YAML machine-checkable structure may be added later.
4. Nightly scheduled audits — assumed acceptable; trivially manual if not.
5. Single-maintainer caveat on OpenChamber originates from third-party review (aireiter, 2026-08), not from OpenChamber's own documentation.

35: 
36: **Document Version:** v1.4
